newsitem.title: USA: Dow shakes off rate woes, sets fourth record of week.
newsitem.headline: Dow shakes off rate woes, sets fourth record of week.

text.p: In one of Wall Street's most volatile sessions ever, blue chip stocks overcame stiff early selling Friday to roar to their fourth record of the week.

The Dow Jones industrial average, which was down nearly 70 points soon after the opening, finished the day with a gain of 78.12 points at 6,703.79, beating Thursday's record of 6,625.67. For the week, it gained 159.70 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,258 to 1,235 on active volume of 545 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index, the New York Stock Exchange Composite and the Nasdaq Composite index all closed at new highs.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 5.82 points to 1,332.02, a record. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks gained 4.65 to 759.50, also a record.
Stocks started the session in a deep hole, put there by strong monthly employment figures from the Labour Department.

The data included a surprising 262,000 increase in non-farm payrolls in December, far exceeding the 190,000 average forecast among economists, and a higher-than-expected 0.5 percent rise in monthly wages.
The report, which suggested the economy remained far stronger last month than many had thought, sent the inflation-jittery bond market into a tailspin and interest rates spiking higher.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost more than a point, boosting its yield to 6.85 percent from 6.75 percent on Thursday. The yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, was the highest since 6.92 percent on Sept. 30. Inflation is a bond investor's worst enemy as it erodes the returns on long-term investments.
Stocks, which initially followed bonds lower, reversed course as investors seized on some of the brighter implications of the news.
"Today was a tale of two markets and, as expected, bonds got clocked," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Stocks were a different story because "the strong report, in conjunction with some of the other numbers we've seen recently, suggests fourth quarter earnings are going to be good," he said.

Stock investors, for whom earnings are at least as important as interest rates, will be treated to the first real sampling of fourth quarter corporate earnings next week, when the reporting season begins in earnest.

The mixed signals on interest rates and earnings produced a rowdy session that saw the NYSE impose index-arbitrage programme trading curbs three times, first because of the Dow's decline and later because of its sharp advance.
The session was only the fourth ever when curbs were applied for both an upswing and downturn on the same day.

In a continuing pattern on Wall Street, investors pounced eagerly on the morning dip, buying technology and economically sensitive stocks such as automobiles and basic materials makers, which would benefit most from a strong economy.
"I think particularly in technology, the view still is to buy every time there's a temporary dip," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
Among Dow components, General Motors Corp. jumped 1-7/8 to 61-1/8, International Business Machines Corp. gained 1-1/8 to 163 and Aluminum Co. of America added 1-5/8 to close at 71-1/4.
Oil shares remained strong, with Exxon Corp. up 2-7/8 to 105-3/4 and Texaco Inc. up 2-3/8 to 107-3/8.
The jump in interest rates hurt bank stocks with Citicorp off 1-1/2 to 100-1/4 and Chase Manhattan down 5/8 to 87-3/4.
United Airlines' parent UAL Corp. fell 1-5/8 to 59-1/8 and American Airlines' parent AMR Corp. lost 1-1/2 to 85-1/8.
America Online Inc. jumped 5-1/4 to 39-5/8 on bullish comments on the company by a Morgan Stanley analyst.
Motorola Inc. climbed 1-5/8 to 66-5/8, as several Wall Street analysts expressed optimism that the company's troubled semiconductor and mobile telephone businesses were finally poised to recover.
Sports Authority Inc. skidded 4-1/8 to 17-1/2 after Alex. Brown trimmed its fourth quarter earnings and sales estimates but reiterated a strong buy rating on the company.
The American Stock Exchange index was up 4.30 to 586.04.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.18 to 400.76, a record. The average share was up 23 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,362.726 up 36.782 or 0.50 percent.
